svg.text: A custom instruction in the pipeline: a cycle of its own
Opcode custom-0. Decoded in DECODE, carried through EXECUTE, computed in MEMORY, written back. Generated from custom/instructions.json by make custom (src/Custom_Unit.sv).
rs2 read only in R format
A = rs1 B = rs2 or the immediate
the same inputs the ALU gets
not used by a custom instruction:
every result side by side, then AND-OR
a > b ? a - b : b - a
the custom result, written to rd
and forwarded to DECODE from here
The custom logic’s cycle: MEMORY_CUSTOM_A/B → CustomUnit → WRITEBACK_DATA. Nothing else uses it, so it cannot slow the rest of the core.
forwarded from WRITEBACK: a dependent instruction waits in DECODE until then (CUSTOM_HAZARD_REGISTER1/2)
What the next instruction waits for (traces of the cycle-exact model, baseline build)
Dashed: held in DECODE. The wait is counted with the load stalls in the cycle equation (hpmcounter3). A compiler hides it the way it hides a load: by putting independent work in between.
Measured with make timing (sky130, logic only): the core alone 3.88 ns; with the four example instructions 4.05 ns, the custom unit’s popcount being the longest path (docs/CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS.md).
